findings.reason: The protected recursive DFS is not valid across the source domain in the app-local Python runtime. On a legal fully reachable 100 by 200 room, it raised RecursionError after cleaning 997 of 20,000 cells. The inert candidate represents the same DFS with explicit [row, col, direction, offset] frames and cleans all 20,000 cells without depending on Python's recursion limit.

The candidate retains virtual coordinates, hash-set discovery, four-direction exploration, and exact physical go-back restoration. Its explicit frame state makes parent suspension and resumption visible, preserves O(c) time and O(c) space, and is conventional iterative DFS rather than a workaround tied to a fixed recursion-limit setting.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium interactive LeetCode problem 489 and the opaque Robot contract. The candidate uses only move, turnRight, and clean; never reads the hidden room or absolute position; starts from virtual coordinate (0, 0) facing source-guaranteed up; returns None; and cleans every reachable empty cell.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065034505 are algorithmically identical recursive coordinate DFS implementations. The candidate preserves their direction order, virtual neighbor calculation, visited-before-entry rule, cleaning point, right-turn schedule, and four-turn physical restoration, but replaces recursive call state with inert explicit frames. Promotion remains separately blocked on authorization and remote Accepted evidence for exact staged native bytes.

The source-legal upward-facing open-room tiers contain 49, 196, and 784 reachable cells, span 16x, and exercise constant-time coordinate membership. The exact candidate passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers. With the scoped 10,000,000-line safety allowance, a correct explicit linear-scan visited control passed every output but failed only runtime with relative growth exponent +0.65 and a 22.53x largest runtime ratio. The 1,205-cell snake also confirms that the candidate succeeds where the protected source raises RecursionError.

The candidate-targeted Approach exactly defines each stack field, the physical-facing invariant, successful-child suspension, blocked or visited advancement, child-pop restoration, parent offset update, and hash-set discovery. Its reachability proof and O(c)-time/O(c)-space analysis match the candidate rather than the unchanged recursive source.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the hidden binary-grid model, complete Robot API behavior, initial upward direction, boundary-wall note, blind custom-testing contract, both examples, the first explanation, all nine constraints, and source section order. The sole source image was independently recreated as an accessible table with the same 5 by 8 layout, walls, and start cell.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order: the exact 5 by 8 illustrated room starting at (1, 3), followed by the one-cell room. The robot-cleaner validator represents the source output by requiring every reachable open cell to be cleaned.

The illegal disconnected-open-cell case was replaced with a fully reachable obstacle layout. Every correctness and benchmark fixture now honors the source's initially-upward direction instead of using invented rotated starts.

Boundaries cover 1 by 1 and 100 by 200 grids, start coordinates (0, 0) and (99, 199), wall and open values, a 1,205-cell recursion-depth snake, corridors, cycles, dead ends, open rectangles, branching layouts, and maximum dimensions.

An independent breadth-first reachability oracle verified every authored and benchmark count and confirmed all open cells are reachable. Both implementations agreed on 1,390 exhaustive connected small-room/start scenarios; the deep snake independently reproduced the protected source's RecursionError while the candidate cleaned all 1,205 cells.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the corrected 7 by 7, 14 by 14, and 28 by 28 open-room workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
